subject.title: browser tool: add force parameter for click and expose evaluate action

question: Should OpenClaw expose a browser click `force` parameter, and if so what operator/model guardrails must make it a last-resort path instead of the default click behavior?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically small, but `force` intentionally bypasses Playwright actionability checks and changes the browser tool’s safety/fidelity contract, which automation should not decide on its own.

options.title: Approve guarded force click
options.body: Add a narrow opt-in `force` field for click/double-click with prompt/tool wording that requires a recorded normal-click failure or equivalent reason, plus focused tests and live overlay proof.

options.title: Keep evaluate as the only escape hatch
options.body: Close or defer the force-click portion and rely on the existing gated evaluate path for exceptional DOM interaction cases.

options.title: Defer for broader browser-action policy
options.body: Leave the issue open until maintainers define a general policy for synthetic browser actions, auditability, and model fallback ordering.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded force click
recommendation.body: Add a narrow opt-in `force` field for click/double-click with prompt/tool wording that requires a recorded normal-click failure or equivalent reason, plus focused tests and live overlay proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sits on the browser click/action surface that steipete recently extended and on the product/security boundary called out in the related evaluate cleanup.
